newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Rural Press says Q1 ahead of yr ago.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rural Press says Q1 ahead of yr ago.

text.p: Regional publisher and broadcaster Rural Press Ltd said on Friday that trading in the first quarter of the year to June 30, 1997 had been slightly ahead of a year ago, though some targets were proving hard to achieve.

"Trading for the first quarter of the current financial year has been slightly above the first quarter of last year, though some targets are proving difficult to achieve," Rural Press Chairman John B. Fairfax told the company's annual meeting.
"The good season across most of the country gives some cause for optimism, but if past years are any indication it will be a slow recovery," Fairfax said.

"We remain positive regarding further progress by your company during the current year, and in the years to come, growing the wealth of shareholders in a secure, sustainable and responsible way," Fairfax said.
In late August Rural Press managing director Brian McCarthy said it would be more difficult to get profit growth in the first half of 1996/97 than in the second half.
Rural Press posted an operating profit of A$52.72 million in the full 1995/96 year and a net profit of A$31.53 million, up six percent.
Rural Press' first half net profit in 1995/96 was A$16.27 million.
Rural Press shares were unchanged at A$4.10 at 12.15 p.m. (0215 GMT).
